# Predicting House Prices with a Simple Decision Tree
Consider predicting house prices based solely on living area. If the only information we have is whether the living area within the house is above or below 150 m², a simple decision tree can be constructed to make predictions. The tree would have a single split at the root node based on the living area feature. If the living area is greater than 150 m², the tree would predict a higher price (e.g., 2.4 million DKK); otherwise, it would predict a lower price (e.g., 1.4 million DKK). This simple structure allows for easy interpretation and provides a clear decision rule based on the living area, as illustrated in @fig-Trees_Simple.

{{< include /Figures/Computational_Statistics/Trees_Simple.qmd >}}

Naturally, this is a highly simplified model that ignores other important features such as location, number of bedrooms, and age. However, it serves as a clear example of how decision trees can be used for regression tasks, where the goal is to predict a continuous outcome (house price) based on a single feature (living area).
:::
